utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. We remind you again of the affirmation, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Yes, I remember that, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Bezruchenko. Do you agree that what you have done in your report, all through your report is in fact to exaggerate the features of what you call an armed conflict, in particular the intensity of the fighting and the organisation and strength of the NLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe my assessments were made on the basis of the sources and documents available to me. I believe that these sources in all their entirety as accurately and carefully analysed would suggest that the NLA organisation was, as such, at least in its main features as I described in my report, and speaking of the intensity of the conflict I do not really see your point, sir. What do you actually mean by exaggerating the intensity of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we'll come to each point in a second, but I have another general proposition to put to you, Mr. Bezruchenko. Do you agree that you have sought to hide or camouflage the criminal or terrorist character of the NLA with a view to make it look like an armed group. Is that correct? Like an army.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That might be your mental construct, Mr. Mettraux, but in fact what I have described in my report are the issues which are not related to crimes, as I mentioned previously. Because had my report been originally intended to cover such issues as criminality, political aspects and negotiations to resolve the conflict, these issues would have been included into the report and reflected in appropriate chapters.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown exhibit number P45 at page 139, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, is it correct that in August 2001, other than the 18 policemen or the -- I'm sorry, the 18 service men who were killed in the mine attack in Karpalak on the 8th of August 2001 and Ljubotenski Bacila on the 10th of August of 2001, no one policeman and no one army man was killed during the month of August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, could you look, please, at the document that is in front of you. That's the "White Book" of the Ministry of Interior. And I will ask the registry to first present page 139, please. That would be the next page, please. It would be page 139, N000-9387. Page 139 of the "White Book", please. Thank you. Mr. Bezruchenko, that's again a list with which you're quite familiar. This is the list of police officers killed during the armed confrontation in 2001. Do you agree that no one police officer was killed during the month of August of 2001, according to that list?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this list, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, again, this is a list with which you are quite familiar. This is the same list as regards the killing of members of the army. And if you can scroll down to the bottom of the page, please, you will see that from number 25 to number 42, I apologise, of the document, that's the next page, there are 18 individuals who were killed in Karpalak and Ljubotenski Bacila and a last one in an unidentified location. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: A number of men were killed in August 2001, that's correct. Whether this number is exactly 18 I cannot really tell because I would have to go to the previous page again and count them one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is it correct that apart from the last person on the list, the circumstances in which this person died are unexplained in this document. All of the deceased from the side of the security forces during the month of August of 2001 died either in the attack in Ljubotenski Bacila or in the attack at Karpalak. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this document, yes. But I don't think this is the only document which deals with the issue of casualties of the Macedonian security forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that both attacks, the mine attacks of the NLA in Karpalak on the 8th of August, 2001, and in Ljubotenski Bacila on the 10th of August of 2001 were condemned as terrorist attacks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that they were also condemned by the international community in particular the United Nations. Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've indicated to the Chamber that on the 13, 1-3, of August of 2001, the Ohrid Framework Agreement, an agreement between the main political parties in the country was signed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, sir, but if you permit me, let me please finish my answer regarding the general issue of casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bezruchenko, at this stage we will move forward and I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I believe not, Mr. Mettraux. Yes, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There are two major sources which address the issue of casualties of the Macedonian security forces which I used in my report. One is this "White Book", which we have just been referring to, and another one is the secret report of the Ministry of Interior for 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when you referred --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the "White Book" which we have just discussed, throughout the conflict between January and August and September 2001, incidentally the casualty list begins from January, the casualties were distributed as follows. Army lost 43 men killed, while police lost 15 men killed. In total, 69 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can I just ask to you indicate, Mr. Bezruchenko, what you are reading from, please.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Essentially, I'm reading from my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I would like to you indicate to the Judges what you have been reading at this very moment, please.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these are the numbers which are added up on the basis of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that what you just read, Mr. Bezruchenko, are notes which have you marked on your binder. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some of those, yes, I was making yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you indicate what document you said is a secret report from the Ministry of the Interior, to which you have referred as an alternative source of information in that respect?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the report of the Ministry of Interior which was covering the period of 2001. But if you allow me to proceed with my answer, Mr. Mettraux, I will say, that the numbers which are suggested by these two sources are at a discrepancy.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The "White Book" says that the number of those injured in the conflict, I mean the army and the police, were about 260. The report issued by the Ministry of Interior suggests that in fact the exact number of the casualties of the security forces was 389. As you can see, there is a significant difference here of almost or perhaps about 100 men each. Let me also add to this the following. In any conflict, there is a certain ratio between those killed, various fatalities and those injured, that is, those who are wounded. Depending on many factors including -- such as types of weapons used, type of terrain, fortifications, type of operations and many other things. And this ratio may be different. Sometimes, and perhaps in most cases, that would be 1, 2, 3, or 4. In extreme cases, it is could be as high as 1 to 13. So it would be logical to assume that, in fact, the actual numbers of those injured in the conflict would be probably higher.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for that and as a follow-up question, are you suggesting that the other documents, what you call the secret MOI document suggested that the police and/or the army had had any of its members killed during the month of August?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the month of August, not, but there are other documents, including media reports which suggest that some people were killed in August, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when you suggest that the figures between the "White Book" and the secret MOI documents vary, were you able to verify which one were accurate?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't really make any specific requests for verification of information with any of the agencies involved, but I would tend to trust more the report of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that what you sought to depict as an armed conflict, Mr. Bezruchenko, was in fact no more than a series of violent sporadic incidents. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tend to disagree with you, sir, for a number of reasons. First of all, this conflict definitely had a cause, and this cause for whatever it was worse, was ultimately reflected in the Ohrid Agreement. Secondly, there were definitely two opposing forces involved in this conflict. They can be described -- they could be described in military terms, they could be described in political terms, and they could also be described in ethnic terms. And this is not only my view. This is only -- this is also the view of Macedonian experts, Mr. Arsovski, Kuzev and Damjanovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you indicated already, Mr. Bezruchenko, that you never spoke to those experts to which you referred many times. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not speak to them but I don't really understand how that might reflect on the contents of the book which is very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D848, please. The ERN would be 1D00-7465, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, what I'm about to show to you is a document which is the result, we understand, of discussion between the Office of the Prosecutor on the one hand and Ambassador James Pardew of the United States of America and we received permission to use this particular document. I would like to read out to you what, Mr. Pardew, Ambassador Pardew the special envoy of the United States to Macedonia had to say about the situation in 2001. Ambassador Pardew believes that: "During 2001 there was not a war in Macedonia on a continuous basis. There were a series of violent incidents, for example, when the NLA took over the Skopje suburb of Aracinovo. There were other incidents as well, but these were individual, isolated events. It was not a situation where there was fighting going on all of the time. But there was always the potential that a higher intensity conflict could break out, like a civil war. So in the summer of 2001, there was a low level conflict where insurgents fought with Macedonian security forces. But the conflict was not yet a 'full blown civil war'." Do you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that as suggested by Ambassador Pardew, what was happening in 2001 in Macedonia was a series of violent, individual and isolated incidents. Do you agree with this analysis on that point?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would rather agree with, in fact, a very succinct, I would say condensed, message that encapsulated this whole paragraph which is expressed in the last two sentences. It clearly says there was a low level conflict where insurgents fought with Macedonian security forces. The key word here in this sentence is "conflict." The next sentence reads: "But the conflict was not yet a full blown civil war," and I absolutely agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for this indication. Are you also in agreement with the suggestion that he made to the effect that this "conflict" as he used this term, was made of a series of violent, individual and isolated events or incidents. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether these were isolated, well, probably would require deeper analysis. If we are talking about geographic isolation, yes, in many cases they were indeed geographically isolated taking place in various locations. However, in geographical sense, there was a strong tendency for all these fronts, Tetovo, Kumanovo, Skopje, Gostivar, Debar, to finally be linked which would present a very serious threat and probably would increase the capabilities of this conflict to move closer to this threshold which would then have constitute the civil war.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for this explanation, Mr. Bezruchenko. Is it correct that what you did, for instance, to bring these events to the point where you could argue or you could conclude in any case, that this was an armed conflict was by exaggerating, for instance, the number of men which you say were members of the NLA during the relevant period and I think you mentioned 8.000 men. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular figure, or, rather, this particular assessment is based on various sources. As I mentioned previously a number of times already, the NLA had huge mobilisation potential. They could easily -- I mean the NLA could easily increase their numbers many times. Some other experts in fact, like again Macedonian experts, tend to believe that the number, the actual number of the NLA, was somewhat lower. For instance, the number which is provided in the book, War in Macedonia by Kuzev, Arsovski and Damjanovski is about, if I recall correctly, 6.000 men. However, I'm afraid this assessment is not entirely correct for the mere fact that the authors do not really mention all the NLA brigades which apparently were not known to them at the time of writing the book. So my assessment is pretty conservative in any case. It is pretty close to the assessment of Mr. Arsovski, Damjanovski and Kuzev. And I don't really think there are any grounds to qualify this assessment as overestimated.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall mentioning Jane's publication as a reliable source of information and in fact relying on various publications of theirs for the purpose of preparing your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: At various stages, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D908, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, what will appear in front of you is an extract or an article, in fact, coming from Jane's Defence Weekly, and it's dated the 29th of August of 2001. It's Rule 65 ter 1D908. The ERN is 1D00-7798. Thank you. And if the registry could scroll down the page to the second half. Thank you very much. Mr. Bezruchenko, I would like to read to you this part of the Article. It says this: "Estimating the number of weapon held by the National Liberation Army, NLA, in Macedonia, is a task beset by difficulties. The size and status of the NLA is a primary question. Notionally organised into six 'brigades', it has claimed a potential strength of 16.000. While this is clearly an exaggeration, it would be prudent to estimate that there are some 2.000 to 2.500 'full time NLA combatants operating in Macedonia.' However, the NLA can also count on the active support of at least many supporters to undertake non-fighting tasks (reconnaissance, patrols, communications, logistics) and who, as a rule do not wear uniforms or carry arms. Almost all of these what might be termed 'second echelon NLA' undoubtedly possess weapons." So do you agree that the estimate that Jane's is doing of the strength of the NLA in -- at the end of the month of August of 2001 is significantly more modest than yours. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would actually draw somewhat different concept from this particular paragraph. What I would say is that, in fact, the emphasis in this paragraph is expressed in the second -- rather, third sentence. Let me read it again. "However the NLA can also count on the active support of at least as many supporters to undertake non-fighting tasks, (reconnaissance, patrols, communications logistics) and who as a rule do not wear uniforms or carry arms. Almost all of these what might be termed second echelon NLA undoubtedly possess weapons." Analysing this paragraph and assuming the number of 16.000 would be the uppermost threshold of this assessment and assuming that the number of 2.000 would be the lowest threshold of this assessment, even arriving at an average figure would give you the number of exactly 8.000 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But the question was much more simple than the answer, I believe, Mr. Bezruchenko. Do you agree that the estimate which Jane's gives of the members of NLA combatant and the number of NLA combatants is much lower than the one which you have advanced here and in your report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Mettraux. I cannot agree with that because it is much more complex than it would appear on the first glance.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct also, Mr. Bezruchenko, that what you have exaggerated in your report is the level of sophistication of an organisation which you sought to attribute to the NLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me read on to you in the same article what Jane's is saying. It says this: "NATO must deal with the fact that the NLA does not have a fully integrated chain of command nor centralised logistics." I will leave aside the logistics on the side because this is a matter that I think you are in agreement with Jane's. But do you agree with their assessment that the NLA has does not have a fully integrated chain of command as of the end of August 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fully integrated is, in fact, a classical military term which is again applied to conventional warfare. I don't think I ever claimed in my report that the NLA had something which could be described as fully integrated chain of command. What I said in my report was that in fact the NLA had hierarchical elements of the command structure in place, which functioned and were functional throughout the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall also making the claim in your report that towards the end or at the end of what you call the armed conflict the NLA was in possession of approximately 20 per cent of the Macedonian territory. This is paragraph 193 of your report. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you ever try to verify that figure, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in fact this figure is based on a number of sources. First of all, the primary source for this assessment was the annual report of the Ministry of Interior for 2001. This is exactly the figure that this report cites.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't the figure in fact, Mr. Bezruchenko, that would be relevant to these proceedings if at all is the fact that at the end of the crisis the NLA was operating in 20 per cent of the north-western part of the territory and not 20 per cent of the Macedonian territory. Isn't that the right figure?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume the report is speaking about 20 per cent of the territory, of the entire territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me first show you what is Rule 65 ter 1D962, please. This is a map, Mr. Bezruchenko, that was part of a document which I believe you have referred to, and you can confirm this which was provided to you by NATO. And the -- I apologise, we don't have it in colour, but the dark areas, not the square ones, but the dark areas represent the areas in which the NLA was active. And as can you see from the table at the bottom, it suggests that it was up to date, at least in July of 2001. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that, Mr. Mettraux, but I don't really think this is the appropriate map to rely on in this particular discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, this --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we are talking about, if I understand your question correctly, we are talking about the overall territory under NLA control and the definition of this control is something which needs to be discussed separately. However, this particular map seems to represent the areas of operation of individual brigades or rather, the zone, approximate zones of operations of these brigades. And I would not really call this document a map, because it is not really a map, it is, rather, a sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that. Would you agree in any case and leaving aside for a second the issue of what control would mean in this particular instance, that just looking at those darkened areas this would be far, far from 20 per cent of the territory of Macedonia. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes I would agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown what is Exhibit P393, please. And I would ask the registry to go to page N005-0650-ET-01.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this is part of a Prosecution exhibit already tendered. You have the front page now in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the registry could go to page N005-0650-ET-01. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Bezruchenko, I'd like to read to you a passage from this document under the heading: Criminal acts tied to activities of members of the so-called NLA. The first sentence say this: "As a consequence of the armed activities of the Albanian terrorist organisation, the so-called NLA, in the course of 2001, in the north-west part of the Republic of Macedonia, 20 per cent of her territory was temporarily occupied." Do you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that in light of the document and in light of this particular statement, the document that I've just shown to you a moment ago, what the MOI was really referring was 20 per cent of the north-western part of the country and not 20 per cent of the entire state of Macedonia. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can we please go to the Macedonian version of this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: With the assistance of the registry, please. I believe this would be N005-0617-34, please.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid my interpretation of this particular fact is differing from yours, Mr. Mettraux. If you read this sentence carefully, you will note that the particular part of the sentence, namely in the north-west part of the Republic of Macedonia, actually refers to the location of the activities of the Albanian terrorist organisation called NLA, as the document says, while 20 per cent refers to "her territory", in this particular case being the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So, Mr. Bezruchenko, were you ever able to verify this number, which you claim, the 20 per cent of the entire territory or is that in fact the sole basis of your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remember various statements, I think one of the witnesses mentioned the number of the villages temporarily occupied by the NLA as well as approximate percentage of territory occupied or controlled by NLA which seemed to be pretty close to this assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't it the fact, or, rather, let me put it that way. At the beginning of today I have suggested to you that what you did, in fact, was to try to exaggerate the importance of the threat posed by the NLA and also I have put to you that you have tried to set aside the criminal and terrorist character of the NLA. I will not go back to the statements that qualify the NLA as a terrorist organisation, but I would like to show what is Exhibit P466 again; that is your report. And I will ask you to turn to page 40, please. That would be page 40 of the report. That would be a few pages further down in the document. I believe four pages further down. Mr. Bezruchenko, I'll ask you to look at paragraph 146 of your report. It would be the previous page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in this paragraph, the issue with which you are dealing with is -- or are the financials of the NLA, and you say that according to a Macedonian government sources, the NLA received financial support from a variety of sources, and you mention extortion of money from the local population and businessperson in Kosovo and Macedonia, contribution from local businesspersons, from former KLA funds, and contributions from the ethnic Albanian diaspora in Europe. And if you look at footnote 222, which you put forward as the source of these conclusions, you refer to a document of 25th of July of 2001, entitled information on the NLA activities in the territory of Macedonia. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would like to show you what is Rule 65 ter 1D873, please. It would be ERN 1D00-7633, please. And 1D00-7611 in the Macedonian. Thank you. Mr. Bezruchenko, do you recognise this document as the document which you cite as authority for your conclusions in the report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the registry please go to page 1D00-7638, please. And if you can scroll down a bit to -- yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to draw your attention to the section which deals with the finance of the NLA, Mr. Bezruchenko, and I will read it out to you. It says this: "The information that we have indicates that NLA is being financed in different ways. Self-financing, extorting money from the local population and businessmen in Kosovo and Macedonia, financial support from the Albanian diaspora, contributions from the local businessmen and population, use of former KLA funds, profits obtained from criminal activities as well as contribution from the Albanian mafia in western Europe." Is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that the report on which you rely to prepare your report and which you cite as authority for your conclusions mentions not four, but six sources of finances for the NLA, two of which you have omitted: One self-financing, whatever that may mean; and, secondly, profits obtained from criminal activities, as well as contribution from the Albanian mafia in western Europe. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, this may be the fact that I did not really mention such thing as profits obtained from criminal activities directly in my report. However, that does not necessarily mean that this is not really generally reflected upon, if you carefully read again the paragraph 146, the very first sentence says: "By extorting money from the local population and businessmen," which by and large I think reflects the other element.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bezruchenko, do you see that this extortion of money is mentioned as a separate item of finances in the list provided by the MOI and that, in fact, there's another part of the item which does not appear to be related to the extortion of money but profits obtained from criminal activities, as well as contributions from the Albanian mafia in western Europe and I will put that proposition to you, Mr. Bezruchenko. Is it correct that your omission of mentioning of this particular aspect of the report, just like your explanation or your suggestion that the Karpalak attack was a matter that could be explained in military term and not in criminal term, is a way to describe what is in effect criminal organisation or a terrorist group as a legitimate military entity. Is that what was attempted, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I think that any link between what is called getting profits from criminal activities and an attack at Karpalak is somewhat misplaced, Mr. Mettraux. These are two entirely different matters. This paragraph speaks about money and financing; Karpalak attack was an ambush. Second point that I would like to make is that to elaborate on this point more and actually to have pretty hard evidence of profits obtained from criminal activities would probably need some additional research. There were various rumours and various allegations of Albanian Mafia and criminal activities and all this and all that. But this report does in the really deal with any specifics of this issue. Regarding the other sources of financing, like extorting money was mentioned in my report because I actually got confirmation of these facts from other sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D813, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as it appears on the screen, Mr. Bezruchenko, is it correct that the NLA was in fact financed to at least two-third of its budget by drug trafficking and sexual exploitation of women. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I say, sir, this is one of the many reports which deals with the general issues of criminality in the Balkans, including the allegations which are expressed in the title of this report. But, you know, sex slavery is something completely different from the subject of my report. I was not really interested and I was not really referring to anything like sex slavery.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Before I show you this document, Mr. Bezruchenko, what do you call a group that is financed by crime, commits crime and is called a criminal or terrorist organisation by the entire world? Would that in fact be a criminal or terrorist group? Would that be a fair summary?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, that would be perhaps a fair summary in a sense -- in a factual sense that many states of the world condemned the violence in Macedonia and described this violence as terrorist. However, this qualification is essentially a qualification which is based on political and legal grounds rather than military grounds. As I mentioned previously, my report was limited in scope and was essentially drafted to cover the precise areas which I described to you in the previous sessions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have exhausted my 45 minutes, I think. However, I would have perhaps another ten minutes or so, but I was given 45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mettraux. Time has expired.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Perhaps as a last matter on this point I have given the indication that we would be assisted if the Chamber would agree that we would tender, formally tender the documentation relevant to this witness perhaps at the end of the day during the last session today which would allow us to provide a clean list to the registry and may assist in the process of tendering at the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Does that produce any problem for you, Mr. Apostolski?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll deal with it in the last session then.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just need a couple of minutes just to get prepared technically, and it is with the assistance of my colleague, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Good day, Witness, Viktor Bezruchenko. My name is Antonio Apostolski, and together with my colleague Jasmina Zivkovic, I'm appearing for Mr. Johan Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said you understood the Macedonian language so I would like to indicate to you that, although you understand the Macedonian language to wait before the questions are translated into English and then you provide your answer, thereby helping the interpreters to better do their job. I wanted to just warn you about it. You were the analyst of The Hague Prosecutor's office until you were engaged as an expert to prove the existence of the military conflict. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, essentially these two functions do not exclude one another. I'm still the analyst of The Hague's Prosecution office.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But on this case, you were engaged by the OTP to prove the existence of the military conflict in Macedonia in 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was engaged to describe the conflict in Macedonia in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. You prepared an expert report about the military conflict in Macedonia in 2001. Did you verify the documents and informations that you used in your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are asking, sir, if I made the evaluation of the credibility of the documents which I used in my report, I will say that, yes, such evaluation was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And the sources were verified and carefully analysed. That is what you said at the beginning of your testimony of today. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to the best of my knowledge and assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: According to you, there was a military conflict in the Republic of Macedonia in 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my assessment, and this is my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. I thank you. In paragraph 1 of the report you say that the report presents a military description of the conflict of the two opposing parties in Macedonia. According to you, opposing parties were the Macedonian security forces and the NLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what my report says, and this is my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Speaking of the NLA, we're speaking about the National Liberation Army.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are speaking about the National Liberation Army, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The National Liberation Army is different than the Kosovo Liberation Army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is different, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In your opinion, these are two different organisations.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in my opinion, these are two different organisations for a number of reasons. They had -- okay, that's fine. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. I think I only needed the response whether in your opinion these two organisations are different. And that is correct, right?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Despite the fact that there was some interaction between various elements of the KLA and NLA apparently, these are still two different organisations.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: They had separate commands. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, they existed at different periods of time. The KLA actually existed mainly in 1999, and later, and, as we know, the NLA came into being or at least made its presence public for the first time as it was ascertained by Macedonian society in January 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So they did not have a common command between them, right, that is what I wanted to know?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, strictly speaking, sir, I don't think that the actual KLA existed in 2001. What existed in 2001 and which replaced the KLA in legal and military perhaps, as well as in factual sense, is the Kosovo Protection Corps and you are very well aware of this fact. So, I don't really think you can talk about the common command between the KLA and NLA in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Is it correct, then, that the NLA had no connection with the Kosovo Guards?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not quite understand, sir, what you mean by the Kosovo Guard. Are you referring to the Kosovo Protection Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I was referring to, the Kosovo Protection Corps.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came across some Macedonian documents in the course of writing my report, including, for example, a statement by Prime Minister Georgievski, which seemed to suggest that there was definitely some sort of interaction between the Kosovo protection corps and the National Liberation Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: These allegations seem to have some ground, though in fact it was not really the primary focus of my report. This would really require a lot of additional research and entirely different focus in terms of documents and analysis and I simply could not do this. It was not really my primary purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you will agree with me that the acronym only of the National Liberation Army and the Kosovo Liberation Army are identical in the Albanian language.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. So you will agree with me that in any event, as well as in your previous -- previous testimony they would have their separate General Staff? I'm now speaking of the Kosovo Liberation Army and the National Liberation Army. You can only -- you can also respond to me briefly with a yes or no only.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I cannot really briefly respond to you because this is an extensive issue which needs some elaboration and qualification. I don't think that such a body as Kosovo Liberation Army General Staff actually existed in 2001. There existed a body which was called the Kosovo Protection Corps and had its own headquarters. Perhaps it was called General Staff. I just do not know. I was not really looking into this matter. But I must mention again, as I mentioned before, there probably was some sort of interaction between KPC, that is Kosovo Protection Corps and the NLA. And, of course this is a common fact which you are aware of that, for instance Mr. Gzim Ostreni served previously in KLA, and then in KPC, and then he became the Chief of Staff of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: That means that the National Liberation Army and the Kosovo Liberation Army could not have their own common archive. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they probably could have a common archive, but, again, it was not really the issue that I was looking at in the course of writing my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: How would it be possible for them to have a common archive if the Kosovo Liberation Army was operational in 1999, while the National Liberation Army in 2001? How is that possible? Could you explain that to me.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just mentioned, sir, that they probably could, which does not necessarily mean that they really have it. On the other hand, I would say perhaps that, as I mentioned, there was some interaction between these two, but whether this archive really exists what kind of speculation existed to this point is really difficult to say. My impression is that there should be some archive which probably reflects many aspects of this conflict from the NLA perspective and perhaps it is still being kept somewhere, but where exactly is difficult to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So that means that the Kosovo Liberation Army and the National Liberation Army had different documents for internal organisation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. It is quite possible in fact that some of the documents and internal regulations which were used by the KLA probably were taken over by the NLA. And in fact, just cursory reading of those documents and comparing these documents with the JNA regulations seems to suggest, at least in very general terms, that they were simply copied and translated from original JNA manuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does that mean that they were not the ones who prepared them? I'm speaking of the documents in possession of the National Liberation Army.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. I think that they were based, by and large perhaps, in -- on experience of fighting in the wider area in the Balkans, including the war in Bosnia and the war in Kosovo and perhaps in part they could be prepared on the basis of specifically fighting in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: During the -- in the course of preparation of your report, you used a lot of sources. You classified the sources in three large categories: Macedonian governmental sources; sources of ethnic Albanians; and international sources. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it true that you were using information also during the interviewing of the witnesses in this case?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is that correct that you were present during the interview of Ali Ahmeti, the supreme commander of the NLA on 30th of July, 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is that true, that you were present at the interview of Gzim Ostreni, the head of the General Staff of the National Liberation Army, on 27th and 29th of July, 2005?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Just for the record in line 17 should -- should be July 2005. Is that correct that you were present at the interview of Nazim Bushi, the commander of 114th Brigade, on 19th and 10th of July, 2004 [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you agree with me that the statements of the above-mentioned persons have the biggest weight in relation to the National Liberation Army?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in terms of evidence for analysis?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I think in the sense that they would be the ones who would be able to tell the real picture of the NLA the best in Macedonia, that these are the most knowledgeable persons.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think their statements were pretty interesting in this respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski, would that a convenient time for you. It is a little early but there is a --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Deal with during the break, and that may delay the Judges a short time in coming back after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there a reason the witness is not here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Okay, that's all right. I assume Mr. Apostolski had some intriguing motion to be heard in the absence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, you previously told me that you were present at the interview of Mr. Gzim Ostreni. Is it correct that during the Gzim Ostreni interview he gave you documents about the NLA?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He gave documents about the NLA to the OTP investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: That was when he was interviewed where you were present. That was the first time you saw the documents. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think this was the first time that I saw these specific documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Before that, you never saw nor you ever got any documents about the NLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Neither the OTP nor you ever found any NLA archive where those documents were kept. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not really involved in any search for NLA archive, if this is what you mean, sir. But I understand that such a thing as NLA archive is not really within the possession of OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: During the interview of Gzim Ostreni, did you ask whether they have an archive?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall if I asked -- or, rather, if the investigator asked this question specifically, but I remember some media reports, for whatever they were worth, that apparently some archive of this nature existed somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you check yourself whether this kind of archive exist?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't really check that. I think such reports were attributed to some Macedonian media, and I think there was a discussion at a later point with my colleagues, and I think also that such search was not really undertaken because the information about the existence, alleged existence, of this archive seemed to be very insufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you think it would be useful to carry out such an investigation, whether the NLA has an archive?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it would.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And that would have surely helped you in preparing your report.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that would.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now list the written documents, based on which you base your report and they are received from sources, as you call them, ethnic Albanians and we will go through them one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 65 ter 778.16. That is the -- about the development of the mobilisation and the formation of the headquarters or General Staff received by Gzim Ostreni [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, this report was received from Gzim Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: At the top we can read: National Liberation Army, General Staff. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that this document is dated 2001, and next to it we can see Major-General Gzim Ostreni?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the document contained no specific date but only the year 2001 is mentioned?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. And I think I already mentioned this fact specifically in my discourse with Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So this -- it was possible that this document could have been prepared any time during 2001.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible, but we should also bear in mind the fact that officially the NLA ceased to exist on 26th September 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: That means that this might have been prepared on 26th of September. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This possibility could not be excluded.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown Exhibit P00459, which has been admitted in evidence. That is the personnel and material formation of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is that true, that have you used this document in preparing your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that this document, as well as the one before it, does not bear a specific date when it was developed, so we could not set the specific date for this document?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think your assessment is reasonable, sir, but what I would also like to add at this point is that this document is essentially - essentially - consistent with the documents provided by other sources, including NATO sources which seem to be suggesting that the general structure of the brigade would be in fact compatible with that as described in various international and Macedonian documents, as it stood in 2001, at least till September.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to stay first with the evidence received by the Albanian sources, and, after that, we will start reviewing the other sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the Exhibit P00460.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure about the number, so if the counsel could please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is -- for the transcript, it's Exhibit P00460.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is formation of personnel and material formation of the infantry battalion. Is it correct that you have used that in the preparation of your report. It is mentioned in the footnote 76.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that this document does not bear a date, other than the year when it was produced?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, sir. This is pretty obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So that means that we can say about this document as well, that it could have been prepared during any time in 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You probably would have some reasons to assume that, sir. Well, but again, I would like to say what I mention in my previous comments on a similar document, the actual structure and strength of the battalions as described by various other sources would seem to suggest that this document perhaps served as the main planning document for formation of battalions in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But, Mr. Bezruchenko, is it correct that you hold the position that if a document does not bear a date, then its evidentiary value is reduced, the weight of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is not a question that is within the scope of this witness's expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: How do you see this as appropriate or within the capacity of the witness to answer, Mr. Apostolski?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the witness please be shown -- this will clarify -- when we show him the next document, it will become clear. So could the witness please be shown the Exhibit P466, the report of Mr. Bezruchenko, the page 64, paragraph 229.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You say that the document bears no date which reduces its significance. Do you see this in front of you?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the Exhibit P00461.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see it in front of you? The regulation on the responsibilities and the operation of the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And this is a document that you had received from Mr. Gzim Ostreni. This is the National Liberation Army. So, is it correct that this document again bears no date. It just bears the year, 2001, but no date?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown also 65 ter 212, ERN R062-6954. Could we now move to the next page in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document as a document you have used when producing your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you agree with me that this document, as the ones before it, just bears the year and there is no date when the document was produced?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, sir. But may I actually offer you a general comment? In fact, all these documents which we have just been discussing are the regulations. Normally, a regulation is in fact quite a lengthy document which can contain from several dozen to several hundred pages, and normally it is limited in circulation. It is either classified or secret, and as it has quite a number of pages, it also has hard cover, like a binder does. This hard cover, the front one, would bear the general title of the institution which would issue this document; in this particular case, obviously General Staff. The title of the document, which in this particular case is personnel and material formation of the brigade, as well as the classification degree which says in this particular case military secret, strictly confidential. It would carry the date, but only the year of issue of this document. As to the exact date, by which I mean the day and month of the document issued, this normally would not really be included in documents of this nature. In some cases that would and in some armies that also would, but as a general rule, if we're speaking about only cover pages, you would never come across any specific date of the action -- document being issued, because this date would be normally verified and confirmed by a signature of the official who is issuing this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you see a date in any other location within the documents, other than on the front page?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not really. But they would hardly be there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Have you seen a document entitled: Law for service in the NLA?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall seeing this document. It's probably not really the law but some kind of regulation.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. I would like to have reviewed the documents that I have shown you before. Could the witness please be shown 65 ter 212, ERN R062-6954. 65 ter 212, ERN R062-6954. In your report, you have mentioned this document. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is the regulations for the criteria involved in the classification of information of importance to the National Liberation Army, which must be kept as military or state secrets and the methods entailed in the preservation thereof.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In your report, you say that although the document stresses in Article 3 that the classification of documents of importance to the NLA and the means of protecting and using it in the organs of government and other associations is regulated by law. Do you see the Article 3? It is in front of you.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please explain to me which governmental bodies are referred to in this Article?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My explanation, perhaps, could be that in fact this document was simply translated and copied from relevant JNA document perhaps, and those who were doing these translations did not really bother to review the translation and revise the document properly. But it is also possible that this document was perhaps issued by the KLA and taken over from NLA from KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you agree with me that the original version in the Albanian language reads UCK?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And the abbreviation for the National Liberation Army is UCK, UCK as well. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Isn't it maybe a document by the Kosovo Liberation Army that was only copy-pasted by the NLA?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is possible. But, among other things that I would like to note about this document, is that Article 1, at least in English translation, in fact as well as in Macedonian one, clearly says National Liberation Army. We know that there was no National Liberation Army in Kosovo. There was Kosovo Liberation Army there.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But the document is written in the Albanian language. Isn't it correct? The original document is in Albanian?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you did not verify this, who has done the translation?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I do not really think I had any reasons to verify, well, who was doing the translation of the document, but I think that our interpreters in fact were aware of the fact that there are two different entities with the same abbreviation, which is the UCK in Albanian. So I think they probably did the correct translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. And you say in paragraph 3 that the one who wrote the Article failed to revise it, so this is probably the reason for the mistake. Is that your assertion?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My assertion was that this document was directly translated from B/C/S in the original version when it was being prepared by somebody in the NLA. So this is my explanation, because it would appear logical to assume that NLA did not really have that many regulations and that many personnel perhaps. We should be very well aware of the regulations of such kind. So these were probably directly translated from relevant manuals which existed in the Yugoslav national army before breakup of Yugoslavia. And whoever of the Albanian ethnic Albanian officers or men who were doing this translation from B/C/S probably did not really revise this article properly. But as it was already in Albanian, I don't really think that the interpreters who were doing the translation from Albanian into English in fact had to do any kind of revision because, essentially, it was a direct translation. I hope I was clear enough, so if I will need to repeat what I said, I can repeat it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I just wish to indicate that in Macedonia the Law on Classified Documents was adopted in 2004, so when this document was published in 2001, then the Law on Classified Documents did not exist. So could the witness please be shown 2D403, 65 ter 2D403. This is an unofficial translation organised by the Defence of the 1st and the 83rd Article of the law. Do you see on the top that this is the Law on Classified Information as published in the Official Gazette of Republic of Macedonia number 9/04. The date is the 27th of February, 2004.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, sir. I agree with you that in fact this particular document does not seem to refer to this specific law, and in fact it would be difficult to imagine that it would, because the NLA, of course, regarded itself as an entity which was outside of official institutions of the state.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So you agree with me that the document before it -- the NLA document that I showed you before, and the Article 3 of the document before, did not refer to the government of the Republic of Macedonia and the law of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apparently not.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go back now to the previous document once again. 65 ter 212, R062-6954. Could we please look at the Article 7 of this document, page 2 in the English version. Could we please show the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see the Article 7 before you? It reads that: "Officers in command structures, staff offices, units and groupings of the armed forces and persons in charge in active and other organisations as well as in state and political bodies are responsible for the proper functioning of the protection of confidential information and are obligated to supervise the taking of protective measures for the information." Can you agree with me that this Article as well indicates that this document does not pertain to the National Liberation Army?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think the cover page for this document says that -- or, rather, the cover for this document says that this document was in the ownership of the National Liberation Army. Well, as to the language of Article 7 and specifically mentioning of state and political bodies, my explanation would be perhaps similar to which I had given for a similar document just a few minutes ago. To my mind, that was probably a translation from the B/C/S, direct translation, which was not edited properly, or perhaps this was the document which was taken over from KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you saying that this document is actually a KLA document that is only used by the NLA?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying perhaps, well, that this document would be used both by KLA and by NLA. And in fact in terms of the functional use, it wouldn't really make any difference, because this document probably was applicable in any situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at Article 10. It's on the same page in English, while in the Macedonian version it's in the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go to the bottom of the English page, please, in the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Article 10 says: "Members of the NLA or persons released from service in the NLA may be relieved of their obligations to protect secrets and may, pursuant to Article 61, paragraph 3 of the Law on Service in the NLA, be authorised to inform the state and other bodies about secret or confidential information only if this is in the interest of the general public." Do you agree with me that a minute ago you said that you never saw a Law on Service in the NLA ranks?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I did not really see this law, so I cannot really comment on this particular paragraph. Perhaps this law exists or existed, at least, but I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When you went through this document, didn't you find it necessary to find this law when preparing your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in fact, I was looking, of course, at the legislation of Macedonia which related to the armed forces and police, but I don't recall finding any specific law related to the protection of state secrets.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please explain pursuant to Article 10, members of the NLA are released from their obligations to protect secrets and -- pursuant to Article -- pursuant to law be authorised to inform the state and other organs. Can you please explain to us which organs, other organs are here in question that the NLA members are authorised to inform?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid I'm not really in a position to comment on which state organs are mentioned in this paragraph, because I was looking, in fact, into the various aspects of the conflict, including the NLA of course, but, as I said previously, I didn't come across in my research any Albanian language documents specifically being called laws related to the service in the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that pursuant to this Article they are obliged to inform the state against which they fought?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could be a supposition, but I'm not really in a position to comment on that properly, because I'm afraid my comments would amount simply to speculation. In fact, to find out what exactly is meant in Article 10, we really have to make additional research.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And in your report -- you base your report on these documents. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was mentioned in my report, among others.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you believed Gzim Ostreni when he submitted you these documents, and you didn't even check the content of these documents. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. I checked the content of the document and I read properly after it had been translated from Albanian into English and this translation was completed quite a long time after the interview of Mr. Gzim Ostreni took place. I included this document in my report on the basis of the fact that its cover page in fact bears the logo and title of the National Liberation Army. Specific points about this documents, like this point which you have just reflected on in -- in Article 10 also caught my attention, and in fact I attributed some of these discrepancies to the fact that apparently the translation, as I mentioned, from B/C/S into Albanian were taken liberally.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could now move to P00461.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Before you, I guess you are able to see the document that you used in preparing your report. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It is a regulation on the competencies and operation of the brigade command. You used this document in your report in paragraphs 120 to 126, and you refer to Articles 196 up to 200 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a mistake in the transcript. It's footnotes from 195 to 200.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that this is a very important document about the organisational structure of the NLA, because you have mentioned it quite some times in your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And, of course, this regulation was used by the NLA brigades. The NLA had six brigades. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you told me a while ago that the National Liberation Army and the Kosovo Liberation Army were two different organisations which did not exist at the same time.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So this document pertains to the NLA?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could pertain to NLA. It could actually be compiled and modified to meet the specific NLA objectives and regulations. I'm sorry there is apparently a mistake in line 7 -- in line 17. It should read as it seems to pertain to NLA, it pertains in fact to NLA. And I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So you're not claiming that it pertains to the NLA. Is this what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I say there is a mistake in line 16. I said it pertains - grammatical mistake there - it pertains to NLA. What I'm saying is that from the cover page it is quite clear that this is the document of the National Liberation Army. It has the logo, it has the title National Liberation Army, it has the signature. But as to the actual -- contents of the document, it is also logical to assume that it could be a product in fact of rehashing, if you wish and revising of similar documents which existed in the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If we could move to page 3 of this document, please. The following page, please. If we could please focus on the third paragraph which starts with: Each and every member. "All members of the brigade command (officers, staff, soldiers) are to carry out their duties and obligations pursuant to the constitution, the Law on Defence, the internal regulations of the UCK, this set of regulations and work plans and instructions from their superiors as set forth in the organisational structure of the UCK." Could you please explain to us, as an expert, the members of the brigade command pursuant to which constitution are bound to carry out their duties and work plans?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that perhaps this particular paragraph, as I mentioned may be a product or may be attributed, rather, to the fact that this document was a rehashed document taken over from the KLA or KPC. But it was apparently used by the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Have you studied this document when you prepared your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course I have seen and read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please tell me to which Law on Defence does this document refer, because if you have read it, you've probably read this paragraph as well.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Well, I do not know which Law on Defence is mentioned here, but I can only perhaps suggest, as I mentioned, that this document was a document which was produced either NLA or the KPC and was used as an internal document in the KPC and then was taken over from KPC by the NLA and was used in the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you haven't made any note about all these issues in your report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I made a note of that the NLA apparently used this document. Well, as to the exact origin of the document, namely whether it was a translation from B/C/S and some old JNA regulations, whether it was produced in KLA, whether it was produced by the KPC, I did not really pursue this line of research because it was not really a matter of high importance. As I mentioned previously, there was a great deal of interaction between Kosovo and Macedonia. There were groups crossing the border, there was a lot of weapons coming from Kosovo, and would also very logical to assume that the weapons brought also included perhaps some manuals or instructions for use of these weapons which could be written in Albanian for easier, as well as a number of regulations which probably were in previous use in Kosovo Liberation Army and in Kosovo Protection Corps. So just to summarize my answer again, I would say that in fact the particular origin of this document was not really very important to me while doing my research. There are many instances in specifically asymmetrical warfare when various rebellion armies would use the regulations taken over from various armies at an advanced stage. Say if you have M-16 rifle in your platoon as the basic weapon, you would also need at least a manual to assemble and disassemble this rifle. If you are going to build a force or brigade size, for instance, you at least need some basic documents as to how this force is to be built and on which basis. These documents could be taken from anywhere, from any army of the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you implying that only the first page has been changed and the rest of the text belongs to the KLA, that it comes from a KLA manual?
