utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be the fact, but I don't really think it doesn't really change much in terms of essence of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you read further down in the document where it starts: "Only under the following circumstances." Do you see that? "Only under the following circumstances may members of the UCK not carry out their orders." And then in the second line it says: "If the order given would mean betraying the UCK, the constitutional order or the country." Is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that NLA was fighting for change of the constitution. Is that your opinion?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that this specific document relates really to the Macedonian constitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me whose constitution it refers to?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It really depends on the origin of the document. That might be the fact that perhaps the document was actually -- but this is again only a supposition, might be actually taken over from KPC which at that stage already was planning the independence of Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you did not put this note into your report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that this particular note did not really deserve any special emphasis in my report because, as I mentioned previously, there was a great deal of interaction between Kosovo and Macedonia, and there was certainly some interaction between the KLA, KPC and NLA, which was manifested in many things, as I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you see anywhere in the documents that you reviewed that the National Liberation Army played a role in the defence of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see page 9 of this document, please. Could we see the following page in the English version, please. Could we go a page back in the English version. I believe it's -- down below it is not visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see now that is point 6, head of the office for information and public relations?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now turn to the next page, both in the Macedonian and in the English version, so we can see paragraph 4. Could we see the paragraph 4? Could we scroll up in the English page, please. Thank you. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So the head of the information and public relations office, according to this document should start and should organise activities in order to clarify the goals and the state principles for the constitutional and legal matters and the role of the UCK in the defence of Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that. And as I mentioned previously, this would be best explained by my assessment that this document apparently was prepared by someone within the NLA -- I mean, within the KLA. But according to other indications, it is also equally reasonable to assume that this document was in fact used by the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you did not put a note about all of this in your report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: About what, Mr. Apostolski, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: That this might have been a document of the KLA taken over by the NLA.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: To state that, Mr. Apostolski, I would definitely need to disregard what is the cover page logo and signatures on this document. It would be perhaps a little bit irresponsible for me to definitely say that this was the document prepared by the KLA or Kosovo Protection Corps without making an additional and serious research into the KLA and Kosovo Protection Corps associated issues. Well, therefore, I limited my analysis actually just to stating the fact that there was apparently some interaction between KLA, KPC, and NLA. In fact, even this interaction is pretty obscure. It is pretty difficult to find any documents which would confirm the exact facts, numbers, personalities involved in this kind of interaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you made your report only based on the cover page of this document, without reading the text further down?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course I read the text further down, Mr. Apostolski. But I think I already mentioned, in fact, that the primary purpose of my report was establishing the fact whether the NLA had any documents and internal regulations at all and whether it used them. And it would appear to -- from my report, if you read it carefully, my view was that the NLA indeed had these documents and indeed used them, but that does not necessarily mean that I should emphasise the fact that the NLA actually was responsible for producing these documents. It might very well be the fact that these documents were simply copied or taken over from relevant documents which existed prior to the establishment of the NLA. But I don't really see how this fact would actually affect another fact, which the NLA apparently used these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Have you seen any order of the NLA that is referring to this document?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: To this particular document? If you could go to the first page perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The first page of your report or of this document?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first page of this -- of this document, sir, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the first page be shown, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Have you seen any order referring to this document?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I have seen an order which was in fact an English translation entitled as order by Gzim -- sorry, order by Ali Ahmeti. In fact, this is 65 ter 926.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So that this is not -- that is not this document.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which 65 ter is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This document bore the 65 ter number beginning with 778.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is your response the one that you haven't seen it?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Apostolski, I think I was answering your question as to whether I have seen any document signed, right? So I --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: My question is whether have you seen any order.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Order, that's right. So trying to answer your question, I'm saying that I have seen the document, 65 ter 926, and it is quoted in my report on page 31, which I think is the order signed by Ali Ahmeti.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go on to page 30 of this document. That is page 28 and 29 of the English version, and 31 of the Macedonian version. We have the right Macedonian version page. Could we also find the appropriate English version. That is it. Telecom supervisor.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could we go on to the next page in both versions. Could we -- could you see paragraph 11 the telecommunications supervisor according to paragraph 11 should monitor test and analyse the telecom systems, in particular those that are at the disposal of the Kosovo Guard. So it comes out that the telecom supervisor of the NLA is supposed to monitor, prepare, analyse and test the telecom systems that are at the disposal of the Kosovo Guard. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, and in fact I don't really find it unusual because I really mentioned previously that apparently this document was prepared on the basis of either relevant KLA or KPC documents. So it was simply taken over by the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You testified previously that the National -- the Kosovo Liberation Army and the Kosovo Guard did not exist at the same time?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we display also the following page of the document, so let's go through it together.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see head of sector for civilian affairs?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And if we can focus on subpoint 3, saying, reading that the head of the sector for civilian affairs and since this is a NLA document, according to you, should -- so the head of the sector for civilian affairs of the NLA should initiate and coordinate the activities of the brigade command and the subordinate units with the organs of local and regional administration for protection of historical and cultural material and values from the liberation war in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this yet another illogical thing in the document?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It maybe appear illogical on the first sight, but I think I mentioned previously that a number of these documents seem to have been based on the experience of the war in Bosnia, as well as specific experience of the war in Kosovo. I think I also mentioned that this document seems to have been a product or in fact if you wish, a compilation on basis of number of sources which could be original KPC documents, as well as translations from the old JNA manuals, and it is really difficult to say what the origin of this document is. It would appear, in fact, that it was probably prepared by someone in the Kosovo Protection Corps, and given the fact that Mr. Gzim Ostreni some while served in the Kosovo Protection Corps, it would also be logical to assume that it was he who brought these documents for the use of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So you also did not mention this comment of yours in your report.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is only a speculation, sir. I cannot really say that this is indeed the fact. What I can only say is that this document was taken over from Mr. Gzim Ostreni, and perhaps he would be in a position to comment more on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But it is your testimony that -- your testimony that he might have brought it, but he might as well have not brought it.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My testimony, sir, would be precisely this: This document is apparently produced by somebody in the KPC. It is also possible that this document was produced on the basis of similar documents which weren't used by the KLA, JNA, and KPC. It would be extremely difficult in fact to establish the fact who produced this document and on basis of what documents, but I would also like to add that, in fact, this document apparently made its way to the NLA and apparently was used by the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Doesn't this connect with -- I apologise, I will rephrase my question. Is my claim about the dates, that I presented to you before, would have no impact about the fact of the origin of this documents and the time of preparation of this document. I was claiming before that there is a -- a problem with the documents, that there is a lack of a date. Would you agree with me on this?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is no specific date in terms of date and month. But there is the date indicating the year apparently the document was released.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could it be possible that these documents were non-existent, these regulations that they might have been prepared later by just preparing later the cover page, whereby the NLA insignia were put?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sometime ago - I can't recall specifically when - I raised an objection about the use of the word or the phrase whether something is possible, and I -- I raise a similar objection today, simply because just about anything in life is possible. But I don't know how that advances the work of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, I think the point Mr. Apostolski seeks to make is very simple and very clear, and I wouldn't interfere with his question on the basis that you have advanced. Carry on, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, could you answer my question?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that this possibility cannot be completely ruled out. But to give a precise answer to your question, in terms of yes or no, I'm not in a position.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, this might be a convenient time since I will be going on to a different document after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We adjourn now. Before we do though, Mr. Mettraux, I'm trying to estimate how long we need to allow for your treatment of exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the concern of the Chamber is to take time from Mr. Apostolski, and this would be also one of our concern, what we could do if it is more practical to the Chamber would be to make a very short and very brief application in writing tomorrow in the course of the day which would also give some time, perhaps, to Mr. Saxon to respond over the weekend, if that is more convenient to the Chamber. If, however, you wish us to make the submissions orally, we believe there is between 20 and 25 documents which we would seek to tender, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, does this cause you concern? It would mean that you may come to re-examine without knowing which documents are admitted or not admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It does cause me some concern, Your Honour, in terms of the preparation for my re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, in that case I may have a counterproposal. What we could do at the break would be to show the list to Mr. Saxon, ascertain with Mr. Saxon whether there's any objection to any of the document, if indeed that is the case, we would only seek at that stage to tender those which are, in effect, challenged by the Prosecution which may allow to speed things up and the Chamber to rule on those at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we're moving down a constructive road; we may not have reached the end of it yet. If Mr. Mettraux and Mr. Saxon and, if necessary, Mr. Apostolski, could consider the matter during the break, to see whether there is going to be any difficulty in the formal motion for admission being delayed either to tomorrow or perhaps being advanced in writing. And we'll hear the outcome of that when we resume --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- which we will do at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski, you might plan this evening to finish your questioning, not to finish but to finish this evening, somewhere a little after 20 minutes to which will allow us time, then, to deal with any issues that may remain over these exhibits, and then you will continue tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do my best, Your Honours, and at 20 minutes to 7.00 I will finish this round of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, do you remember that we reviewed together other documents originating from the NLA, Mr. Gzim Ostreni submitted them to you, and we noticed that there was no date on them.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Those are the documents bearing no numbers and no names?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's also right, sir. Actually --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please go ahead, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that it is possible that on those documents only the cover page was replaced?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you mention that these documents bear no numbers and no names. In fact, they bear no numbers but they bear names. As I mentioned previously it is very much possible, perhaps, it can't really be ruled out that the cover page was replaced, but the fact of the matter is that there are sufficient reasons to believe that these documents were actually in use by the NLA, despite the fact that they might have been produced elsewhere. And, of course, I could not really disregard the fact that we obtained these documents from the chief of General Staff of the NLA, who claimed that these were the original NLA documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you did not see a list of members of the so-called NLA brigade?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to any specific brigade, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I am asking you in general about all brigades.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid this is not entirely correct, sir. I have seen the personnel lists, or, rather, the personnel rolls I think of 113 Brigade, as well as units of some other brigades which clearly bear the names of the personnel, their dates of birth, their origin of birth, and other basic data. And I think I quoted the relevant documents in my report, which you have probably seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were the names of the soldiers within the brigade ranks included in those lists?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In some of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you say more specifically which brigades were the ones regarding which you have seen the roles of soldiers and positions?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you give me one minute, I would probably do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am specifically referring to Exhibit 65 ter number 664, which is the NLA document 113th Brigade, Izmet Jashari, which appears to contain the ranks of the personnel, and in fact I have the relevant portion of the report in front of me now and I could probably read the names of these ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Have you seen such a list for the 116th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me to be more specific, no, I didn't see such lists for the 116th Brigade, and there is a very clear reason for this fact, which is really on the surface. The fact for this -- I mean, the reason for this fact is that the 116th Brigade was apparently formed at a very late stage of the conflict, sometime in July 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I apologise, I will rephrase the question. Have you seen the list for the 114th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen the full list of personnel for the 114th Brigade, but in fact there is quite an extensive list of the members of this brigade in various command positions, which can be derived from some Macedonian documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you have not seen a list of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not seen the list of soldiers of this brigade as such.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters have difficulties hearing the Defence counsel so if the microphone could be moved closer to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said yesterday when cross-examined by my colleague Mettraux in the page of 7609, page of the transcript, that the 112th, 113th, 114th Brigade were established in November. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no this is a mistake. They could not be established in November.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I apologise. I might have misspoken or maybe the interpretation was incorrect. I was referring to the month of June.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see. Well, I think the 112th and 113th Brigades were established in fact before June. 114th Brigade was most probably established in the second half of June. But they could not be established in November, no way.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm telling you, Witness, that it is probably a mistake in the interpretation of my question. My question quoted the month of June. So your evidence is that towards the end of June, the 114th Brigade was established and its commander was Nazim Bushi. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could qualify my previous answer a little bit. I think all these brigades were in the process of being formed and they were in fact at various stages of being formed in June 2001. Some of them were perhaps better prepared and they were at more advanced stage of formation than others. I think that in fact the process of formation of the 114th Brigade started sometime in June and perhaps the bulk of the brigade, or at least some significant fighting nucleus of this brigade was established in the second June -- I mean, in the second half of the June of 2001, and indeed the commander of this brigade was Nazim Bushi.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yesterday, when asked by my colleague Guenael Mettraux at page 7109 of the transcript, when asked him which were the brigades operational in June you said 112th, 113th and 114th. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: And 115th was probably forming sometime in end June 2001, early July 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. I would like to go back to the statement of Mr. Nazim Bushi.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the statement of Nazim Bushi, 65 ter 2D00-365, dated 9th and 10th of June, 2004, page 2 of the English version, and page 3 of the Macedonian. Paragraph 4. Do you see it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It was your evidence previously that this gentleman, Nazim Bushi, could give the most reliable testimony on that. In paragraph 4 of the statement he says: "I needed about a week to complete the establishment of the 114th NLA Brigade and that was at or around 8th of June, 2001 -- July, 2001 that the brigade was officially established. I was appointed the commander of the 114th Brigade." Could the next page of the English version be shown, please. "I was appointed as the 114th Brigade commander and promoted to NLA colonel at the same time. The headquarters of the brigade was set in Nikustak." So, according to Nazim Bushi's testimony, can it be inferred that the 114th Brigade was established in July, which does not correspond to your evidence and to your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, actually it does and it does not. But I don't really think it is really possible to be so specific regarding the exact day of the establishment of the brigade. You should really realise that this is a process, not really a momentaneous action which can be completed in one day. I think what we really have to pay attention to in this statement is the fact that the brigade formation process apparently was completed on 8 July. What I was saying was that the brigade formation, by and large, and at least its nucleus was apparently formed by end of July -- sorry, June 2001 or at least in the second half of June 2001. You cannot really expect a brigade which normally under the full formation would have several thousand men to be mobilised assigned to the units, trained and made combat-ready within one day or one week. It is extremely difficult and impossible undertaking, even under those conditions. So I think we have to be flexible with these dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So that means that Nazim Bushi, when saying that he established the brigade within a week, was not speaking the truth. Is that what you, as a military expert, are saying?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying that he was not speaking the truth. I am only saying that the brigade could not be formed within one day. It probably implies that the brigade formation started sometime, or at least some preparatory ground was made for that in June, whereas the actual process was completed in early July 2001, and I don't really think in such matters as formation of such a size of brigade one week really matters much.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In the summary of your report, in the part NLA strategy and tactics at the 41st page, you say that all sources were investigated agree that throughout the conflict the NLA managed to establish control over some specific parts of localities populated predominantly by Albanians mostly in the northern and western Macedonian. My question is: Is it correct that the NLA had no city under its control?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that the NLA had any cities under its complete control.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that no railway station was under the NLA control?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, not under physical control.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In that part of the report, you are saying which part of the territory was under the NLA control and you stated previously to my colleague that it amounted to 20 per cent of the territory of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown a map of Macedonia, P467.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, until the map is displayed, I would ask you a few more questions. You went to the Republic of Macedonia quite often. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I visited Macedonia several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You know the territory of the Republic of Macedonia very well.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really say that I know the Republic of Macedonia very well, because my visits to Macedonia were essentially limited to Skopje and the village of Ljuboten. But I cannot really say that I really know the Republic of Macedonia very well. I mean, the territory of Republic of Macedonia very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: As a military expert, you also have good orientation in using maps. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think I should.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark the territory under NLA's control in mid-May 2001. Please mark it.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would be perhaps easier to describe the territorial control of NLA in terms of the number of the villages which were under the NLA control, but I would imagine that several distinct areas were more or less under NLA control, one would be this area here, more or less along the border; the other area would be here; the other area would be --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: My question referred to the month of May.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. Then this is -- then must be corrected. Maybe we should try it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Apologise, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think in May the NLA control basically extended in some areas above Skopje, as well as some areas above Tetovo; there were also developments with NLA activities in the north of Kumanovo. And that was about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And the other border would be the border of the Republic of Macedonia, just to make it clear for the record.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. And there were no Macedonian security forces in this territory, the territory that you marked, and that is in the period of May 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: But to answer this question, Mr. Apostolski, we would probably have to go to the definition of the territorial control. I'm not saying that the NLA literally had physical control over all this territory. Of course, there were Macedonian security forces, there were border posts, there were army units and there were also police units which were operating in the same areas. But what I'm suggesting is that most of the rural areas, mountainous areas were quite accessible for the NLA to move around and to execute their operations. And most of those villages in fact, predominantly with the Albanian population were indeed in the hands of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you testified about the percentage of the territory.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. But if you recall, I was referring to a number of documents, specifically the report of the Ministry of Interior for 2001, which we extensively described with your learned colleague Mr. Mettraux and which we mutually, I think, agreed upon to the effect that the report clearly speaks about 20 per cent of the Macedonian territory under NLA control in September 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: As far as I am able to notice -- I apologise, we're now speaking about the month of May, right? You marked a NLA-controlled territory during the month of May. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And your testimony is also that the village of Kuceviste, north of Skopje was under NLA control?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. I think, first of all, this map, not really the entirely proper map for indication the areas of the NLA control. And this is in fact a geographical map, a relief map rather than military map, and of course you know, using this map I can make only a very approximate delimitation of the territory which was under NLA control. I don't even see without glasses this village.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I say again, this is very approximate areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: As a military expert, you have surely seen, as I can see here also, you have marked that the road between Kumanovo and Presevo was marked here. I'm not an expert, but can I see that. Could you be more precise -- a little bit more precise, please?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can correct that. It should be probably here. But there was activities in -- in fact, would it be possible to magnify this map a little bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please correct it first and then we will ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We can't magnify it without losing what is marked, so that correct what is there ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Something like this, I would imagine.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you also mark on the map, since I asked about mid-May, could you please put down 15th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't think the date given was the 15th, Mr. Apostolski, but perhaps the witness can indicate whether there is a specific date that this relates to.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you just write down May.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this could be probably end of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would seek to tender this photograph in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The map will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 2D75.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: On this same map, could you mark in red the control that the NLA had -- in your view, the NLA had on 12th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if this is entirely possible for one simple reason, that in fact there was no continuous front line and some of the villages were under NLA control, some of them were not. So drawing a line which would really represent the front line, as such, would be, I'm afraid, a pointless exercise.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could it be of help if the northern part of the map is enlarged?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I could actually do, perhaps to help you, sir, just give you the names of the villages which were apparently under NLA control at various stage of the conflict and I think most of them were under the NLA control by the date of 12th August 2001, and I think these villages are mentioned in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you mark the villages or the areas that were under NLA's control?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am afraid this is not really entirely appropriate map for this kind of exercise, sir. As I mentioned, this is not a topographical military map. This is a geographic map which is more appropriate for a school, rather than for military analysis. This is in fact --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Well, this is the map that we received from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's perfectly all right, sir. But, again, as I'm saying this is not a military map.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: As far as I was able to understand your testimony, the NLA controlled 20 per cent of Macedonia's territory. I would simply like to ask you to mark those 20 per cent of the Macedonian territory.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid, sir, this is a little bit simplistic interpretation of this exercise.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown P487. Your Honours, bearing the time in mind, maybe it would be better if I leave these questions for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It might give you time to identify a map that would show in more detail the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I found it, Your Honours, but we will have not enough time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I found the evidence, I identified the map in question that was -- that was identified by the witness as a military map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, if you haven't enough time to deal with the issue you're concerned with, we'll leave that until tomorrow. Is there some other matter you can conveniently deal with now, or would you prefer to conclude today's questioning at this point?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would end now, and I would give up my time for my colleague Mr. Mettraux and Mr. Saxon to deal with the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Apostolski. Well, Mr. Bezruchenko, we're going on, I believe, to deal with matters of exhibits, so that we can allow you to leave now with a view to your returning to continue tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Have a nice evening, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mettraux, I hope we've left time enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: More than enough, I believe, Your Honour. I'm happy to be the messenger of a good news for once. We used the time at the break with Mr. Saxon to go through the list of proposed exhibits and from the 20 original ones, we ended up with 16; we withdrew one of common accord. There remains two, Your Honour, which will need your specific decision and perhaps I will start with those that do not give rise to any issues between the parties and I will list them in order. The first one would be Rule 65 ter 1D932. Rule 65 ter 1D929 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we need to deal with each in turn and if could you indicate quickly what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very well. Your Honour, the first such document, Rule 65 ter 1D932 is a press release concerning a meeting of the so-called Security Council of the Republic of Macedonia dated 10 August of 2001, which refers, you will recall, to "firm actions."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be 1D249.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document is Rule 65 ter 1D929. This is a document which come from an embassy which we've identified during a private session which is dated the 10th of August 2001, and refers to a meeting between the ambassador of that country and the president Mr. Trajkovski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be exhibit number 1D250.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document Your Honour is Rule 65 ter 1D531. This is a press report, or, rather a collection of a number of press report dated 19 January of 2005, which relates to the role of the president in the events of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be exhibit number 1D251, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The next document is Rule 65 ter 1D928.1. This is dictionary of military terms which has been used quite extensively with the witness we indicated to Your Honour that the original numbering was 1D928. We've added one page which was used with the witness and we would seek to tender the amended version of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is this the United States joint services publication?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be exhibit number 1D252, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The next document is Rule 65 ter 1D957. This is a press report concerning the events of Vejce dated 28th and 29 of April of 2001, in relation to which Mr. Bezruchenko commented in his report and the content of that report in particular, statement attributed to a number of politicians were put to him. It is dated the 29th of April of 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be exhibit number 1D253, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The next document is Rule 65 ter 1D955. This is a press release of 20 March 2001 coming from the foreign affairs committee of the European parliament which refers to the activity during that month of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be exhibit number 1D254, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document is Rule 65 ter 1D952, Your Honour. This is the executive summary of the ICG, the International Crisis Group. It's dated 5 April 2001, and it's called the Macedonian question: Reform or rebellion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be exhibit number 1D255, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Next document, Your Honour, is Rule 65 ter 1D725. This is the actual report of the ICG also dated 5 April 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be exhibit number 1D256, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Next document, Your Honour, is Rule 65 ter 353.18. This is a situation report of 8 August 2001. This was an attachment to the statement, the OTP statement of Mr. Matthiesen. This is a report about the mine attack on the 8th of August of 2001 in Karpalak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be exhibit number 1D257, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document is Rule 65 ter 1D879. This is an address of the president of the government of the Republic of Macedonia, Mr. Ljubco Georgievski dated 21st of March 2001, before the South-east European Cooperation Process Conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be exhibit number 1D258, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The next document, Your Honour, is Rule 65 ter 1D866. This is an unclassified document coming from an embassy which we have identified and it is entitled government security relinquish yet another village. This relates to the events of Aracinovo, Your Honour, and it's dated the 14th of June, 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be exhibit number 1D259, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Next document, Your Honour, is Rule 65 ter 1D908. This is an article taken from Jane's Defence Weekly called how many weapons in Macedonia. This is it dated the 29th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be exhibit number 1D260, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next document is Rule 65 ter 9D -- I'm sorry, 1D959, this is a Presidency statement on the ambush of FYROM soldier. This again relates to the events of Vejce on the 29th of April of 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be exhibit number 1D261, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Next document, Your Honour, is Rule 65 ter 1D881. This is a press article which contains a statement attributed to Ambassador Pardew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be exhibit number 1D262.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Was there a date for that, Mr. Mettraux?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will verify the date in a second. While it's being checked, Your Honour, I will indicate the two documents which will give rise to litigation between the parties and this would be Rule 65 ter 1D554.1 and Rule 65 ter 554.2. As per the previous document, Your Honour, 1D881, the date is 15 of March of 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, the two documents that are at issue in the present case are 1D554.1, is a letter written by a representative of the Defence of Mr. Boskoski addressed to the Macedonian authority and more specifically to the Ministry of the Interior requesting of those authorities to check whether any of eight persons mentioned in the letters were or received in -- between August of 2001 and the end of the month of September of 2001 any salaries from the Ministry of the Interior. The next document, document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The date of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This would be the 30th of May of 2007, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The next document, 1D554.2, is the actual response by the Ministry of the Interior through the state secretary and it is dated the 5th of June of 2007, which indicates that none of the people in question received salary from the MOI or, I believe, appeared on the list of the MOI during the period August to September of 2001. Your Honour will recall that the eight names which appeared on the letter sent by the Defence and thus which were the subject of the response by the Macedonian authorities appeared on a list of receipt given in the police station Cair in the few days that preceded the events that are the subject of these proceedings. In the view of the Defence, we believe that these documents should be admitted at this stage. We believe that Mr. Bezruchenko and we submit that Mr. Bezruchenko gave evidence in particular in his reports about the events inside the village of Ljuboten. He is also making a number of claims in his report to the effect that the people involved were members of the MOI calling, for instance, making a reference, for instance, to what he calls and I quote: "Tarculovski and his police unit" -- paragraph 513 and 522 -- talking of police ground attack or formations of police at paragraph 517 and again, polices attack at paragraph 518. Mr. Bezruchenko has also given evidence about what he says are the disciplinary obligations of the Ministry of Interior and about the fact that such obligation would only exist or arise in relation to de jure members of the ministry. Mr. Bezruchenko has also given evidence about efforts or the lack thereof, made by the Office of the Prosecutor to verify whether the people appearing on this list - and Your Honour will remember - another list were made. Your Honour will recall also that Mr. Bezruchenko took part in several interviews with people who were identified on two such lists, including one person, Mr. Ljupco Savov who appeared on the list relevant to those two letters. Your Honour will recall also that Mr. Bezruchenko originally indicated that he could not remember having seen the list or not this particular list but that through the statement of Mr. Savov, the investigator notes more precisely, it was clear that the list had been presented to the person in the -- or had been the subject of questioning in any case with Mr. Savov in the presence of Mr. Bezruchenko. In view of that fact, Your Honour, we believe there is a sufficient basis to admit this document at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the two documents, 65 ter 1D554.1 and 1D554.2 really need to be looked at together to demonstrate their relevance. However the Prosecution's primary objection is to 65 ter 1D554.2 which is the response of an official from the Ministry of the Interior to a representative of the Defence in this case. Your Honour, the Prosecution believes that the issue here is not what Viktor Bezruchenko discussed or not in his amended expert report. It's much simpler than that. The issue here is that this information from a -- which was put in a letter from an official of the Ministry of the Interior is being submitted to demonstrate the truth of its content. This letter, Your Honours, in the Prosecution's submission is effectively a witness statement and therefore that witness should be called to provide his evidence about this point so that that evidence can be tested and certainly the Defence can do that during the Defence case, if there is a Defence case. Therefore, Your Honour, such letters have been tendered for admission a number of times already in the case and it's to my understanding that these letters have not been admitted in the past. And the Prosecution does not see any stark difference between this letter and other letters whose admission has been rejected by the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In the Chamber's view, Mr. Mettraux, neither letter should be received as an exhibit. They can be marked for identification, if you wish, but the -- the primary objection being to the response, it seems to the Chamber, that clearly the content of that response is a matter which ought to be the subject of more appropriate proof and the first letter really goes with the response.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. We would be grateful if they could be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, exhibit number 65 ter 1D554.1 is marked for identification as exhibit number 1D263, while 65 ter 1D554.2 is marked for identification as exhibit number 1D264. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, if I may be permitted, at page 69, line 7, the record refers to Rule 65 ter 1D625, I must have misspoke. It was Rule 65 ter 725, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. We will, as it turns out, adjourn now and resume tomorrow at 9.00. I don't believe in this courtroom. I think we may be back to Courtroom II.
